note: Questions from the CBSE Class X English (Language and Literature) board exam 2026, Q.P. code 2/1/1, published by CBSE at cbse.gov.in. Model answers are written for this portal and are not CBSE's official marking scheme.

questions.subject: English
questions.text:
Read the following text :
(1) Pancakes, a beloved breakfast dish across the world, has a surprisingly long and diverse history. Archaeological evidence shows that people were cooking pancake as food as far back as 30,000 years ago on hot stones and primitive griddles.
(2) In ancient Greece and Rome, pancakes were made from wheat flour, olive oil, honey, and curdled milk. They were often served as a sweet treat during festivals or special occasions. In medieval Europe, pancakes became a popular dish during Shrove Tuesday, the day before Lent began. In France, thin crepes became a national delicacy, often filled with sweet or savoury ingredients. In Russia, blinis were made using buckwheat flour and served with sour cream or caviar. In Ethiopia, the spongy injera became a staple food, made from teff flour and used as both a plate and utensil. Similarly, in China, pancakes are often savoury while in Japan, fluffy "soufflé pancakes" have become a modern favourite.
(3) The American version of pancakes, thick and soft, gained popularity in the 18th century. The use of baking powder made them light and airy, and they were often served with butter and maple syrup – a symbol of hearty comfort food. Over time, pancakes became a universal dish, symbolizing community and celebration. Whether sweet or savoury, thick or thin, every culture has found a way to adapt this simple food to its own taste and traditions.
(4) India has its own rich tradition of similar dishes that have been enjoyed for centuries. Across the country, almost every region has a version of a pancake – whether sweet or savoury – made from grains, pulses, or rice. These Indian pancakes not only satisfy hunger but also reflect the diversity of India's culinary culture. In South India, dosas and adai are the most famous forms of pancakes. Made from a fermented batter of rice and lentils, dosas are crisp and light, while adai is thicker and more filling. The fermentation process adds a unique sour flavor and makes them nutritious and easy to digest. In Kerala, the appam, made with fermented rice batter and coconut milk, is soft in the center and crispy at the edges. Moving north, we find the western style cheela, a simple and wholesome Indian pancake made from gram flour, spiced with onions, chillies and coriander. In Maharashtra, the thalipeeth is a multigrain pancake that uses flours like jowar, bajra and rice mixed with spices and vegetables. It is both flavorful and filling, providing a good balance of carbohydrates and proteins.
(5) In the eastern parts of India, pitha is a traditional pancake made during festivals and special occasions. Varieties like patishapta in Bengal are sweet, filled with coconut and jaggery. In Assam and Odisha, pithas can be steamed, fried, or roasted, depending on the custom and region. In the western deserts of Rajasthan and Gujarat, people prepare chilla and handvo, which are savoury western pancake-like dishes baked in traditional ovens. These pancakes are a blank canvas for toppings, waiting for a splash of fruit or a scattering of condiments.
(6) Today, pancakes continue to evolve with new recipes, from vegan and gluten-free varieties to those infused with fruits, oats, or even protein powder. Despite their many forms, they remain a timeless reminder of how food connects mankind through shared history and creativity. Each pancake tells a story of regional identity, food traditions and a deep love for food that brings people together. Pancakes are warm, edible hugs that are a perfect comfort on a bleak day.

Answer the questions :
I. In paragraph 1, what does the phrase 'has a surprisingly long and diverse history' mean ? (1)
II. The uniqueness of the spongy injera is that ______. (A) it is both a savoury and a sweet (B) it can be used for cooking and also for eating (1)
III. How are American pancakes made light and fluffy ? When did the American-style pancakes gain popularity ? (2)
IV. True or False : Every culture has adopted the pancake and tempered it with its own ingredients, flavour and taste. (1)
V. Which pancakes are made using the fermentation process ? (A) Dosa and appam (B) Chilla and thalipeeth (C) Blinis and soufflé (D) Pitha and patishapta (1)
VI. The phrase 'a blank canvas' (paragraph 5) means : (A) Like a painter starts with a blank canvas, a diner can get creative. (B) Pancakes reflect the 30,000 old lineage of being the first food. (1)
VII. List any two points that support the statement 'pancakes are a timeless reminder of how food connects people.' (2)
VIII. The phrase 'warm, edible hugs' refers to : (A) comfort food that provides a sense of emotional security (B) the pancake that represents the history of the region (C) the choice of eating hot steaming pancakes (D) the food that gives you energy (1)
questions.solution: I. Pancakes have been eaten for a very long time (about 30,000 years) and in many different forms across the world, more than one might expect. II. (B): injera is used as both a plate and a utensil (it is eaten too). III. Baking powder makes them light and airy; they became popular in the 18th century. IV. True. V. (A). VI. (A). VII. Any two: every culture has adapted pancakes to its own taste and traditions; each pancake tells a story of regional identity and food traditions; a shared love for food brings people together; they keep evolving creatively while sharing a common history. VIII. (A).

questions.subject: English
questions.text:
Read the following text :
(1) Rate of Internet Reach in India : 2014-2024. The rate of internet reach in India rose over 52% in 2024 from about 14% in 2014. Although these figures seem relatively low, it meant that more than half of the population of 1.4 billion people had internet access that year. This also ranked the country second in the world in terms of active internet users.
(2) Internet availability and accessibility. By 2021 the number of internet connections across the country tripled in urban areas because of a higher density of population leading to an increase in the number of connections. However, despite of incredibly low internet prices, internet usage in India has yet to reach its full potential. Lack of awareness about the internet in India persists, especially in rural areas and among women, driven by digital divide, infrastructure limitations, and a lack of perceived need for the internet. This hinders digital adoption, with many not knowing how to use the internet or even being aware of its existence. Targeted awareness campaigns and digital literacy programs are crucial to bridge this gap and ensure people understand and can benefit from the digital ecosystem.
(3) Digital living. Home to one of the largest bases of netizens in the world, India is abuzz with internet activities being carried out every moment of every day. From information and research to shopping and entertainment to living in smart homes, Indians have welcomed digital living with open arms.
Rate of Internet Reach in India : 2017 – 24.0%, 2018 – 28.5%, 2019 – 33.7%, 2020 – 43.4%, 2021 – 46.3%, 2022 – 48.1%, 2023 – 51.5%, 2024 – 52.4%, 2025 – 55.3%.

Answer the questions :
I. What does the term "active internet users" convey ? (A) Active people who use internet (B) Active people who use active internet (C) People who use active internet (D) People who use internet actively (1)
II. Assertion : India is home to one of the largest bases of netizens in the world. Reason : Lack of awareness and a tangible gender gap lie at the heart of the matter. (A) Both true, reason explains assertion. (B) Both true, reason does not explain assertion. (C) Assertion true, reason false. (D) Assertion false, reason true. (1)
III. Identify the word that indicates that internet reach is 'comparatively' low. (Paragraph 1) (1)
IV. Based on the table, which time period shows the maximum internet usage ? (A) 2017 to 2020 (B) 2023 to 2025 (C) 2020 to 2023 (D) 2019 to 2022 (1)
V. Identify one reason why there are fewer internet users among women. (1)
VI. Fill in the blank : Infrastructure limitations ______ (impedes/spurs) digital adoption. (1)
VII. Complete with a suitable reason : An increase in the number of connections in urban areas is because of ______. (1)
VIII. Which are the two ways to bridge the gap of digital unawareness ? (2)
IX. How does the author justify the statement, 'Indians have welcomed digital living with open arms' ? (1)
questions.solution: I. (D). II. (B): both statements are true, but the lack of awareness does not explain why India has so many netizens. III. relatively. IV. (B) 2023 to 2025 (the highest reach, 51.5% to 55.3%). V. Lack of awareness, driven by the digital divide (or a lack of perceived need). VI. impedes. VII. a higher density of population. VIII. Targeted awareness campaigns and digital literacy programmes. IX. Indians use the internet constantly, for information and research, shopping, entertainment and even living in smart homes.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Complete the message from Yogita to her friend Shobit : Dear Shobit, Let's meet at 5 p.m. for the rehearsal but I need to go home first as I ______ anything since morning.
questions.solution: 'Since morning' up to now takes the present perfect: 'have not eaten'.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Identify the error and supply the correction in the sentence from a self-help book : To identifying your goal is the biggest step in your success story.
questions.solution: Error: To identifying. Correction: Identifying (or 'To identify').

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Yamini asked her friend Shifa, "Would you like to come for my birthday party tomorrow ?" Report Yamini's question correctly.
questions.solution: Yamini asked her friend Shifa if/whether she would like to come for her birthday party the next day.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Complete the newspaper clipping : The verdict is yet to come since the members of the jury ______ divided in their opinion.
questions.solution: The subject is 'the members' (plural), so 'are'.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Read Somil's request to his mother : "Can you teach me to swim ?" Report Somil's request by completing the sentence : Somil asked his mother ______.
questions.solution: if/whether she could teach him to swim.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Identify and correct the error in the line from a critical review of a play : 'As an actor, Ravi Raj, is superior then any other contemporary actor.'
questions.solution: 'Superior' takes 'to', not 'then' (or 'than'): 'superior to any other actor'.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Complete the line from the 'Rules and Regulations' section of a school diary : Minimum 75% attendance is ______ to appear for the final examinations.
questions.solution: A rule requiring attendance: 'mandatory' (compulsory).

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Complete the newspaper report on a proposal by a Member of Advisory Board : After the meeting it was obvious that most stakeholders would not support ______ proposals.
questions.solution: 'Proposals' is plural, so the plural demonstrative 'these' fits (referring to the member's proposals).

questions.subject: English
questions.text:
Attendant : Did you have your dinner, sir ? Passenger : Yes, thank you!
The flight attendant asked the passenger ______. The passenger replied in affirmation and thanked him.
questions.solution: if/whether he had had his dinner.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Complete the sentence from the memoir of your grandparent : 'When I was the team Captain, I ______ often organise get-togethers to develop bonding among the team mates.'
questions.solution: 'Would' expresses a repeated habit in the past.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Complete the sentence about the reaction of a tourist to another : Yesterday you loved the spicy Indian curry, ______ you ?
questions.solution: A positive statement in the simple past takes a negative tag with 'did': 'didn't you?'

questions.subject: English
questions.text:
Student : What prompted you to become a professional writer ?
Writer : My childhood library housed books of all kinds. I was fascinated with the compelling stories and wanted to create my own.
Report the student's question.
questions.solution: The student asked the writer what had prompted him/her to become a professional writer.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: You are Divya/Divij Kumar, Director, Nurturing India, an organization providing skill education to youth. You believe that today's youth needs vocational and skill education that will encourage an independent and entrepreneurial lifestyle. Write a letter to the editor of a local daily expressing your views on the need and importance of skill education in creating employability and a self-employed independent generation.
questions.solution: Format (1 mark): sender's address, date, The Editor and newspaper, subject (Need for skill education for youth), salutation, close, name and designation. Content (2 marks): many graduates lack job-ready skills; vocational training (IT, electrician, tailoring, design, agriculture-based skills) improves employability; it encourages entrepreneurship and self-employment, reducing dependence on scarce jobs; it supports national schemes such as Skill India and NEP 2020; an appeal for skill centres, industry tie-ups and awareness. Organisation and accuracy (2 marks).

questions.subject: English
questions.text: You are Nirmala / Nirmal, a resident of Jhunjhunu Colony. Recently there have been a series of accidents and petty crimes in your colony. One of the reasons is poor street lighting. Write a letter to the Commissioner of the Works department, drawing attention to the urgent need to install street lights to avoid further crimes and accidents.
questions.solution: Format (1 mark): sender's address, date, The Commissioner, Works Department, subject (Urgent need for street lights in Jhunjhunu Colony), salutation, close, name. Content (2 marks): many streets are dark at night; recent accidents and petty crimes (chain-snatching, thefts); women, children and the elderly feel unsafe; request to install and maintain street lights quickly, possibly solar LED lights, and to repair broken ones. Organisation and accuracy (2 marks).

questions.subject: English
questions.text: "Improvements in sports infrastructure with a focus on multi-purpose sustainable facilities as well as the integration of technology along with a grassroot centric approach is the key to bring Indian athletes on the world stage." Write an analytical paragraph on the above statement in about 120 words, expressing your views on how improved infrastructure can help Indian athletes win accolades for the nation.
questions.solution: Introduction: India has great sporting talent, but world-class results need world-class facilities. Analysis: multi-purpose, sustainable stadiums and training centres let many sports share resources and reach more athletes; technology such as performance analytics, video analysis and sports science improves training and prevents injuries; a grassroots approach spots talent early in villages and schools and gives it coaching and nutrition. Examples: success in shooting, wrestling and athletics after better support. Conclusion: with improved infrastructure and early support, Indian athletes can win more medals and bring glory to the nation. Marks: content 3, accuracy 2.

questions.subject: English
questions.text:
Read the following details about the characteristics of the Indian start-up ecosystem :
1. one of the most vibrant and largest in the world.
2. drives innovation across various fields.
3. brings unique solutions to major challenges both domestic and international.
4. has entered various fields – healthcare, e-commerce, agriculture.
5. supported by funding and government initiatives.
In about 120 words analyse the future of startups in India considering factors that have supported its growth in the country. Focus on aspects of the need, benefits, and support needed for these startups.
questions.solution: Introduction: India's start-up ecosystem is among the largest and most vibrant in the world. Analysis: start-ups drive innovation and offer new solutions to problems at home and abroad, in healthcare, e-commerce, agriculture and more; they create jobs and attract investment. Growth has been supported by funding and government initiatives such as Startup India, digital infrastructure and a young, tech-savvy population. Needs: easier access to capital, mentoring, simpler regulations and support beyond big cities. Conclusion: with continued support, the future of Indian start-ups is bright, and they can power economic growth. Marks: content 3, accuracy 2.

questions.subject: English
questions.chapter: First Flight: Nelson Mandela – Long Walk to Freedom
questions.text:
Read the extract and answer the questions :
We have, at last, achieved our political emancipation. We pledge ourselves to liberate all our people from the continuing bondage of poverty, deprivation, suffering, gender and other discrimination. Never, never, and never again shall it be that this beautiful land will again experience the oppression of one by another. The sun shall never set on so glorious a human achievement.
(Nelson Mandela – Long Walk to Freedom)
I. What is the tone Nelson Mandela is UNLIKELY to have used in his speech ? (A) inspirational (B) assertive (C) conflicted (D) direct (1)
II. According to Mandela, emancipation is not merely political. Elaborate. (2)
III. Fill in the blank : Mandela's speech swings between references to the past and a ______ (bleak/promising) future. (1)
IV. Explain the sentence, "The sun shall never set on so glorious a human achievement." (1)
questions.solution: I. (C) conflicted. II. Political freedom is only the first step; Mandela pledges to free his people from poverty, deprivation and suffering, and from gender and other discrimination, so that freedom becomes social and economic as well. III. promising. IV. The end of apartheid is so great an achievement that its glory will last forever and never fade.

questions.subject: English
questions.chapter: Footprints without Feet: The Book That Saved the Earth
questions.text:
Read the extract and answer the questions :
OOP : I haven't a clue. I've been to seven galaxies, but I've never seen anything like this. Maybe they're hats. (He opens a book and puts it on his head.) Say, maybe this is a haberdashery!
OMEGA : (bowing low) Perhaps the Great and Mighty Think-Tank will give us the benefit of his thought on the matter.
THINK-TANK : Elementary, my dear Omega. Hold one of the items up so that I may view it closely. (Omega holds a book on the palm of her hand.) Yes, yes, I understand now. Since Earth creatures are always eating, the place in which you find yourselves is undoubtedly a crude refreshment stand.
OMEGA : (to Iota and Oop) He says we're in a refreshment stand.
OOP : Well, the Earthlings certainly have a strange diet.
(The Book that Saved the Earth)
I. "Elementary, my dear Omega." What is Think-Tank's tone in the sentence ? (A) patronising (B) admonishing (C) ironic (D) sarcastic (1)
II. Why does Omega call Think-Tank great and mighty ? (2)
III. Fill in the blank : After viewing the book closely, Think-Tank concludes that Earth creatures ______ (enjoy/dislike) eating food. (1)
IV. Why does Oop open the book and put it on his head ? (1)
questions.solution: I. (A) patronising. II. Think-Tank is the vain, self-important ruler of Mars who insists on being flattered; Omega addresses him as 'Great and Mighty' out of fear and to please him, which also shows his arrogance and conceit. III. enjoy (he thinks they are always eating). IV. He has never seen a book and guesses it might be a hat, so he tries it on.

questions.subject: English
questions.text:
Read the extract and answer the questions :
Some say the world will end in fire some say in ice.
From what I've tasted of desire
I hold with those who favour fire. (Stanza 1)
But if it had to perish twice,
I think I know enough of hate
To say that for destruction ice
Is also great
And would suffice. (Fire and Ice)
I. Complete : According to Robert Frost, fire refers to ______. (1)
II. Why does the poet believe both fire and ice can destroy the world equally ? (2)
III. Fill in the blank with one word : In the line "But if it had to perish twice", 'it' refers to the ______. (1)
IV. Select the option with the same rhyme scheme as the lines in Stanza 1 (ice / desire / fire) :
(A) They are all gone away, / The House is shut and still, / There is nothing more to say.
(B) Tell me not, in mournful numbers, / Life is but an empty dream! / For the soul is dead that slumbers.
(C) The dog chased the ball down the lane, / He ran with such incredible speed, / His tail was a blur, a joyful glee.
(D) The Sun is high, / The clouds drift past, / In the blue sky which is so vast. (1)
questions.solution: I. desire (greed, passion). II. Fire stands for desire and ice for hatred; uncontrolled desire consumes people quickly like fire, while hatred slowly makes people cold and insensitive like ice. Both lead to conflict and destruction, so either is enough to end the world. III. world. IV. (D): stanza 1 rhymes abb (desire/fire), as do past/vast in option D.

questions.subject: English
questions.chapter: First Flight: How to Tell Wild Animals
questions.text:
Read the extract and answer the questions :
Though to distinguish beasts of prey
A novice might nonplus,
The crocodile you always may
Tell from the Hyena thus :
Hyenas come with merry smiles
But if they weep they're crocodiles.
(How to tell Wild Animals)
I. What is the most likely reason the poet uses the word 'nonplus' instead of 'confused' ? (1)
II. Explain the irony in the last two lines of the stanza. (2)
III. Fill in the blank with one word : The word 'novice' signifies a/an ______ person. (1)
IV. What kind of atmosphere is created through these lines ? 1. humorous 2. mysterious 3. aggressive 4. confusing 5. fearful. (A) 1 and 4 (B) Only 5 (C) 1, 2 and 3 (D) 4 and 5 (1)
questions.solution: I. To keep the rhyme (nonplus / thus) and add humour. II. Smiles and tears usually show happiness and sorrow, but here the 'merry smiles' of the hyena and the 'tears' of the crocodile belong to dangerous predators: the hyena's laugh is its call, and 'crocodile tears' are false. Seemingly friendly or sad signs actually warn of danger. III. inexperienced. IV. (A) humorous and confusing.

questions.subject: English
questions.chapter: First Flight: A Letter to God
questions.text: Lencho's last letter to God depicts astute faith on one level and irony on the other. Bring about the element of faith and irony in the situation. (A Letter to God) Answer in 40–50 words.
questions.solution: Lencho's faith in God is so strong that he never doubts God sent the money. Ironically, the postmaster and employees who kindly collected the seventy pesos are called 'a bunch of crooks' by Lencho, who believes they stole the missing thirty pesos. His unshakeable faith in God is matched by distrust of the very people who helped him.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: "Mijbil the Otter" sensitises human beings especially city people to wildlife. What emotions are conveyed through the association of Mijbil and Maxwell ? Answer in 40–50 words.
questions.solution: The story conveys deep affection, trust and care. Maxwell treats Mijbil like a child, playing with him, bathing him and worrying for him during the difficult journey to London. Mijbil in turn becomes attached and playful. Their bond shows that wild animals can share love and that humans should treat them with understanding.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: What is the contribution of the extended metaphor in the poem "Fog" ? Answer in 40–50 words.
questions.solution: Carl Sandburg compares fog to a cat throughout the poem. Like a cat, the fog comes silently 'on little cat feet', sits looking over the harbour and city 'on silent haunches', and then moves on. The extended metaphor vividly conveys the fog's quiet, mysterious arrival, stillness and departure.

questions.subject: English
questions.chapter: First Flight: Madam Rides the Bus
questions.text: How does "Madam Rides the Bus" bring alive Valli's attributes and experiences through its narrative style ? Answer in 40–50 words.
questions.solution: The story is told from Valli's point of view, with vivid descriptions and lively dialogue. We see her curiosity as she watches the street, her careful planning and saving, her confidence and dignity with the conductor, and her joy at the scenery. The sight of the dead cow then shows her maturity. This style makes her experiences real.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Explain why time is probably one of the most valuable possessions that one intensely regrets losing. (The Ball Poem) Answer in 40–50 words.
questions.solution: Like the boy's ball, which bounced into the harbour and could not be bought back, time once lost never returns. As the boy stares 'all his young days into the harbour', he realises that childhood, too, is passing. Money can replace objects but not time or memories, which is why losing it brings deep regret.

questions.subject: English
questions.chapter: Footprints without Feet: The Making of a Scientist
questions.text: Working through his project of collecting and tagging butterflies, Ebright developed a scientific temperament. Elaborate. (Making of a Scientist) Answer in 40–50 words.
questions.solution: From collecting butterflies and raising thousands of monarchs to tagging them for Dr Urquhart's migration research, Ebright learned to observe carefully, ask questions and run real experiments. After losing a science fair, he realised he had to do experiments, not just display things. This curiosity and method made him a scientist.

questions.subject: English
questions.chapter: Footprints without Feet: The Midnight Visitor
questions.text: Mention how Ausable was always one step ahead of everyone. (The Midnight Visitor) Answer in 40–50 words.
questions.solution: When Max held him at gunpoint for the secret papers, Ausable calmly invented a story about a balcony below his window and complained that the police often entered through it. When knocking was heard, Max, believing the police had come, jumped out of the window onto a balcony that did not exist. Ausable's presence of mind outwitted him.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Mention any two reasons that substantiate that Bholi's mother was a negative presence in her life. (Bholi) Answer in 40–50 words.
questions.solution: Bholi's mother neglected her because of her pockmarked face and stammer, considering her a burden. She agreed to send her to school only to get rid of her, and she happily accepted a marriage proposal from the old, lame, greedy Bishamber for Bholi, without regard for her feelings or future.

questions.subject: English
questions.chapter: First Flight: A Tiger in the Zoo / The Tale of Custard the Dragon
questions.text: Examine the similarities and differences between the tiger in "A Tiger in the Zoo" and the dragon in "The Tale of Custard the Dragon". Answer in 100–120 words.
questions.solution: Both are powerful, fearsome creatures confined to small spaces: the tiger in a concrete cage, Custard in a little red wagon. Both are judged by appearances and kept in roles that do not show their true nature. The differences are clear. The tiger is full of quiet rage and longs to roam the forest, hunt and terrorise villages; the poem is serious and protests against caging wild animals. Custard, though he looks fierce with teeth and spikes, is thought to be a coward, but bravely kills the pirate when danger comes; the poem is humorous and shows that real courage appears when needed. One shows the pain of captivity, the other the irony of appearances.

questions.subject: English
questions.chapter: First Flight: The Sermon at Benares / For Anne Gregory
questions.text: "The Sermon at Benaras" and "For Anne Gregory" deal with the themes of 'love' and 'life'. Discuss. Answer in 100–120 words.
questions.solution: In 'The Sermon at Benares', Kisa Gotami's love for her dead son makes her seek a cure for death, but she learns from the Buddha that death is common to all; life is subject to decay, and wisdom lies in accepting it rather than clinging to grief. In 'For Anne Gregory', Yeats shows that human love is often based on outward beauty, like Anne's yellow hair, and that only God can love a person for herself alone. Both texts look beyond the surface: the Buddha teaches that attachment brings suffering and peace comes from understanding life, while the poem suggests true love should value the inner self.

questions.subject: English
questions.chapter: Footprints without Feet: A Triumph of Surgery
questions.text: Evaluate how "A Triumph of Surgery" is a lesson in thoughtful parenting. Answer in 100–120 words.
questions.solution: Mrs Pumphrey loved her dog Tricki like a child but spoiled him with excessive food, sweets and little exercise, so he became fat, lazy and ill. Her love lacked discipline and good judgement. Herriot took Tricki to his surgery, gave him no medicine but plenty of water, a simple diet and exercise with other dogs, and he recovered. The story teaches parents that love must be balanced with discipline; indulging every wish can harm children. Thoughtful parenting means caring about long-term health and well-being: proper diet, activity and limits, not just pampering. Mrs Pumphrey's 'triumph of surgery' was really a lesson in sensible care.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Evaluate how "The Necklace" critiques the obsession with appearances and social status. Answer in 100–120 words.
questions.solution: Matilda Loisel is unhappy with her modest life and longs to appear rich and admired. To impress others at a ball, she gets an expensive dress and borrows what she thinks is a diamond necklace. When she loses it, pride stops her from telling Mme Forestier the truth; instead the couple buy a replacement on huge loans and spend ten years in poverty. In the end she learns the necklace was fake. Maupassant shows how valuing appearances and status over honesty and contentment leads to ruin. The fake necklace symbolises the hollowness of social show, and the story warns that vanity and pretence can cost people their happiness.
